title: Introduction to Computer Science
description: Fundamentals of programming, algorithms, and computational thinking using Python. Covers variables, control flow, functions, data structures, and introductory object-oriented programming.
syllabus: Week 1-3: Python Basics and Variables. Week 4-6: Control Flow and Functions. Week 7-9: Data Structures (Lists, Dicts). Week 10-12: OOP Fundamentals. Week 13-15: Final Project.

lessons.title: Setting Up Your Environment
lessons.content: Install Python 3.11 and VS Code. Configure your PATH and verify with python --version. Create your first hello_world.py script.

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types
lessons.content: Python supports int, float, str, bool. Variables are dynamically typed. Use type() to inspect. Practice with arithmetic operators and string concatenation.

lessons.title: Chapter 1-2 Reading
lessons.content: Read 'Think Python' chapters 1-2 covering program structure, values, and variables.

lessons.title: Conditionals and Loops
lessons.content: if/elif/else statements. for loops with range(). while loops. break and continue. Nested loops for matrix traversal.

lessons.title: Functions and Scope
lessons.content: Defining functions with def. Parameters vs arguments. Return values. Local vs global scope. Default parameters and *args.

lessons.title: Control Flow Demo
lessons.content: Watch the recorded demonstration of building a number guessing game using loops and conditionals.

lessons.title: Lists and Tuples
lessons.content: Creating and manipulating lists. Slicing, appending, sorting. List comprehensions. Immutable tuples and when to use them.

lessons.title: Dictionaries and Sets
lessons.content: Key-value pairs. Dictionary methods. Set operations (union, intersection). Choosing the right data structure.

title: Calculus I
description: Limits, derivatives, and integrals of single-variable functions. Applications to physics, economics, and optimization problems.
syllabus: Week 1-3: Limits and Continuity. Week 4-7: Derivatives and Rules. Week 8-10: Applications of Derivatives. Week 11-14: Integration. Week 15: Review and Final.

lessons.title: Introduction to Limits
lessons.content: Intuitive definition of limits. One-sided limits. Limits at infinity. Squeeze theorem with examples.

lessons.title: Continuity
lessons.content: Definition of continuity at a point. Types of discontinuities. Intermediate Value Theorem and applications.

lessons.title: Definition and Basic Rules
lessons.content: Limit definition of derivative. Power rule, product rule, quotient rule. Practice computing derivatives of polynomial and rational functions.

lessons.title: Chain Rule and Implicit Differentiation
lessons.content: Composite functions and the chain rule. Implicit differentiation for curves. Related rates problems.

lessons.title: Derivative Visualization
lessons.content: Interactive video showing how derivatives relate to slope of tangent lines and rate of change.

lessons.title: Antiderivatives and the Fundamental Theorem
lessons.content: Indefinite integrals. The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus parts I and II. Basic integration rules.

lessons.title: Techniques of Integration
lessons.content: U-substitution. Integration by parts. Partial fractions for rational functions.

title: World History: 1900 to Present
description: Survey of major global events, movements, and transformations from the early 20th century through today. Emphasis on interconnected political, social, and economic developments.
syllabus: Week 1-3: World War I and its aftermath. Week 4-6: Interwar period and Rise of Totalitarianism. Week 7-9: World War II. Week 10-12: Cold War Era. Week 13-15: Post-Cold War and Globalization.

modules.title: The Great War and Its Aftermath

lessons.title: Causes of World War I
lessons.content: Alliance systems, imperialism, militarism, and nationalism. The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and the chain of declarations.

lessons.title: Treaty of Versailles
lessons.content: Terms of the treaty, reparations, territorial changes. Seeds of future conflict. The League of Nations.

lessons.title: WWI Documentary Clips
lessons.content: Selected clips from 'They Shall Not Grow Old' showing trench warfare and its human cost.

lessons.title: Rise of Fascism
lessons.content: Mussolini in Italy, Hitler in Germany, militarism in Japan. Economic conditions enabling authoritarian movements.

lessons.title: The Global Conflict
lessons.content: European and Pacific theaters. Key battles: Stalingrad, Midway, D-Day. The Holocaust. Atomic bombings and surrender.

lessons.title: Superpower Rivalry
lessons.content: US vs USSR ideological divide. NATO and Warsaw Pact. Nuclear arms race. Containment policy and proxy wars.

lessons.title: Decolonization
lessons.content: Independence movements in Africa and Asia. The Non-Aligned Movement. Lasting effects of colonial boundaries.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: Structure, bonding, and reactivity of carbon-based molecules. Nomenclature, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms, and spectroscopy. Laboratory techniques included.
syllabus: Week 1-2: Bonding and Molecular Structure. Week 3-5: Stereochemistry. Week 6-8: Substitution and Elimination. Week 9-11: Addition Reactions. Week 12-14: Carbonyl Chemistry. Week 15: Final Exam.

lessons.title: Atomic Orbitals and Hybridization
lessons.content: sp3, sp2, sp hybridization. Sigma and pi bonds. Molecular orbital theory basics. Bond angles and geometry.

lessons.title: Functional Groups
lessons.content: Alcohols, ethers, amines, carbonyls, carboxylic acids. Naming conventions (IUPAC). Physical properties and polarity.

lessons.title: Chirality and Enantiomers
lessons.content: Chiral centers. R/S configuration using Cahn-Ingold-Prelog rules. Optical activity. Racemic mixtures.

lessons.title: 3D Molecule Viewer
lessons.content: Interactive video demonstrating stereoisomers using 3D molecular visualization software.

lessons.title: SN1 and SN2 Reactions
lessons.content: Nucleophilic substitution mechanisms. Substrate structure, nucleophile strength, solvent effects. Rate laws and stereochemistry outcomes.

lessons.title: E1 and E2 Elimination
lessons.content: Elimination reactions competing with substitution. Zaitsev's rule. Hofmann elimination. Reaction coordinate diagrams.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Advanced programming concepts including linked lists, trees, graphs, sorting algorithms, and algorithm analysis. Prerequisites: Intro to CS.
syllabus: Week 1-2: Algorithm Analysis (Big-O). Week 3-5: Linear Structures (Stacks, Queues, Linked Lists). Week 6-8: Trees and Heaps. Week 9-11: Graphs. Week 12-14: Sorting and Searching. Week 15: Final Project.

lessons.title: Big-O Notation
lessons.content: Asymptotic analysis. O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2). Best, average, worst case. Space complexity.

lessons.title: Recursion
lessons.content: Recursive function design. Base cases and recursive cases. Stack frames. Fibonacci, factorial, and Tower of Hanoi examples.

lessons.title: Binary Search Trees
lessons.content: BST properties. Insertion, deletion, search operations. Balancing: AVL trees introduction. Time complexity analysis.

lessons.title: Graph Representations
lessons.content: Adjacency matrix vs adjacency list. Directed and undirected graphs. BFS and DFS traversal algorithms.

lessons.title: Tree Traversal Animation
lessons.content: Animated walkthrough of inorder, preorder, and postorder traversals on sample binary trees.

lessons.title: Comparison-Based Sorting
lessons.content: Merge sort, quicksort, heapsort. Divide-and-conquer strategy. Stability. Lower bound of O(n log n) for comparison sorts.

lessons.title: Linear-Time Sorting
lessons.content: Counting sort, radix sort, bucket sort. When and why they beat the comparison lower bound.

title: Introduction to Psychology
description: Overview of psychological science covering perception, learning, memory, development, personality, social behavior, and mental health.
syllabus: Week 1-2: History and Methods. Week 3-4: Brain and Behavior. Week 5-7: Learning and Memory. Week 8-10: Development. Week 11-13: Social Psychology. Week 14-15: Mental Health and Therapy.

lessons.title: History of Psychology
lessons.content: From Wundt's lab to modern cognitive neuroscience. Behaviorism, psychoanalysis, humanism, and cognitive revolution.

lessons.title: Research Methods
lessons.content: Experimental design, correlational studies, case studies. Variables, controls, ethics in research. Replication crisis.

lessons.title: Classical and Operant Conditioning
lessons.content: Pavlov's experiments. Skinner box. Reinforcement schedules. Extinction and spontaneous recovery.

lessons.title: Memory Systems
lessons.content: Sensory, short-term, and long-term memory. Encoding strategies. Forgetting curves. Eyewitness memory reliability.

lessons.title: Memory Experiments Demo
lessons.content: Video demonstrations of classic memory experiments including the serial position effect and change blindness.

lessons.title: Social Influence
lessons.content: Conformity (Asch). Obedience (Milgram). Groupthink. Bystander effect. Persuasion techniques.

lessons.title: Attitudes and Prejudice
lessons.content: Attitude formation and change. Cognitive dissonance. Implicit bias. Stereotype threat. Reducing prejudice.
